about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice B): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Gaeng Som Southern Thai Sour Fish Curry
recipes.summary: A thin, sharp and fiery orange curry of white fish and vegetables with no coconut, tangy with tamarind.

items: 600g firm white fish fillet, cut into chunks

steps: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Stir the curry paste into the water in a pot and bring to a boil until the water turns deep orange.
Add the tamarind, fish sauce, sugar, carrot and cabbage and simmer for 8 minutes until the carrot is tender.
Add the beans and fish and simmer gently for 5 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily at 63°C.
Taste for sour, salty and sweet balance and serve in bowls with the rice.
notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish and shellfish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Gaeng Panang Thai Peanut Beef Curry
recipes.summary: A thick, mild, sweet-salty coconut curry of tender beef with peanut and lime leaf.
steps: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Simmer half the coconut milk with the curry paste in a wide pan for 5 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the beef, fish sauce and sugar and cook 5 minutes, then stir in the remaining coconut milk, peanut butter and lime leaves.
Simmer for 10 minutes until the beef is tender and reaches 71°C, adding the capsicum for the last 4 minutes.
Spoon the curry over the rice, spoon the thickened coconut cream from the top of the pan and serve while hot.
notes: Food safety: cook the beef to at least 71°C. Contains peanuts, fish and shellfish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Kai Palo Thai Five-Spice Egg and Pork Stew
recipes.summary: Hard-boiled eggs and pork belly in a sweet five-spice broth, served over rice with pickled greens.
steps: Hard-boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
Simmer the pork in the water with soy sauce, sugar, five-spice, garlic and fish sauce for 30 minutes until the pork is tender and reaches 70°C.
Add the eggs and simmer for 10 minutes until the eggs are tinted brown and the sauce is glossy.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy and serve with the stew spooned over.
notes: Food safety: simmer the pork to at least 70°C and hard-boil the eggs. Contains egg, fish, gluten and soy. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Or Lam Luang Prabang Smoky Eggplant Stew
recipes.summary: A Lao stew of pork, eggplant and beans thickened with ground rice and perfumed with dill.
steps: Crush the garlic, shallots and chillies to a paste.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Simmer the pork in the water with the paste and fish sauce for 20 minutes.
Add the eggplant and ground rice and simmer for 10 minutes until the eggplant is tender and the stew thickens.
Add the beans for the last 4 minutes, check the pork reaches 70°C and is tender, then stir through the dill.
notes: Food safety: cook the pork to at least 70°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Nom Banh Chok Khmer Fish Gravy Noodles
recipes.summary: Fresh rice noodles with a lemongrass and turmeric fish gravy and a platter of raw herbs and vegetables.
steps: Simmer the fish in the water for 8 minutes until opaque and flaking at 63°C, then flake it apart.
Blend the fish with the lemongrass, turmeric, garlic and ginger to a rough paste.
Return to the pot with the cooking water, fish sauce and coconut milk and simmer 12 minutes until thick.
Cook the noodles until tender, about 4 minutes, and drain.
Pile the noodles into bowls, ladle over the gravy and serve with the cucumber, sprouts and mint.
notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Shan Khao Swe Burmese Chicken Noodles
recipes.summary: Noodles in a mild tomato and turmeric chicken sauce, topped with crisp garlic and pickled greens.
steps: Fry the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes until golden.
Add the turmeric, tomatoes and chicken and cook 6 minutes, stirring.
Pour in the water and fish sauce and simmer 15 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C and the sauce thickens.
Cook the noodles until tender, about 4 minutes, and divide into bowls.
Spoon over the chicken sauce and scatter with peanuts and coriander.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C in the centre. Contains peanuts and fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Ohn No Khao Swe Burmese Coconut Chicken Noodle Soup
recipes.summary: The signature Burmese coconut chicken noodle soup, golden and soothing, topped with boiled egg and chilli.

items: 600g chicken thigh fillets, cut into chunks

steps: Hard-boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool and peel.
Blend the onion, garlic and ginger, fry in a pot with the turmeric for 5 minutes.
Add the chicken, stock, coconut milk and fish sauce and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir the chickpea flour with 1/4 cup cold water, add and simmer 5 minutes until the soup thickens.
Boil the noodles until tender, about 4 minutes, divide into bowls, ladle over the soup and top with halved eggs and lime.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C in the centre and hard-boil the eggs. Contains egg, gluten and fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Canh Chua Ca Southern Vietnamese Sour Fish Soup
recipes.summary: A sweet-sour tamarind soup of fish, tomato and pineapple with sprouts and herbs.

items: 500g firm white fish fillet, cut into chunks

steps: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Bring the water, tamarind, garlic, fish sauce and sugar to a simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and pineapple and simmer 4 minutes.
Add the fish and cook gently for 5 minutes until opaque and flaking at 63°C.
Stir through the sprouts and coriander and serve with the rice.
notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Nasi Goreng Kampung Anchovy Fried Rice
recipes.summary: Village-style fried rice with chilli, anchovies and greens, topped with a fried egg.
steps: Crush the shallots, garlic and chillies to a paste.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok and fry the paste and anchovies for 2 minutes.
Add the beans and rice and fry on high for 5 minutes, stirring until piping hot, then add the kecap manis.
Fry the eggs in the remaining oil until the whites are set.
Top each serve with an egg.
notes: Food safety: use rice that was chilled within 1 hour of cooking, reheat until steaming hot, and fry the eggs until the whites are set. Contains egg, fish, gluten and soy. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Bak Kut Teh Klang Herbal Pork Rib Soup
recipes.summary: A peppery garlic and herb pork rib soup, simmered long and eaten with rice and dark soy.
steps: Blanch the ribs in boiling water for 5 minutes, drain and rinse.
Simmer the ribs in the 8 cups water with the garlic, spice mix, soy sauce and pepper for 75 minutes until the meat is tender and reaches 70°C.
Add the tofu puffs and simmer 8 minutes.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy and blanch the bok choy for 2 minutes.
Serve the soup with the rice, bok choy and the dark soy for dipping.
notes: Food safety: simmer the ribs until tender and at least 70°C. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Chilli Prawns Singapore Sweet-Tangy Style
recipes.summary: Prawns in a sweet-tangy tomato chilli sauce with a ribboned egg, mopped up with rice or buns.
steps: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Fry the garlic, ginger and chillies in the oil for 1 minute, then add the prawns and cook 3 minutes until pink and curled.
Stir the tomato sauce, sweet chilli sauce, cornflour and water together and pour in, simmering 2 minutes until glossy.
Stir the beaten egg slowly into the sauce and cook 1 minute until it forms ribbons and sets.
Spoon the prawns and sauce over the rice, scatter with the remaining egg ribbons and serve while hot.
notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque, at least 63°C inside, and the eggs until set. Contains egg, shellfish and gluten. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Tinolang Manok Filipino Ginger Chicken Soup
recipes.summary: A clear ginger and chicken soup with green papaya-style chayote and leafy greens, plain and restorative.
steps: Fry the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil for 4 minutes until fragrant.
Add the chicken and fish sauce and cook 4 minutes.
Pour in the water and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C.
Add the chayote and simmer 8 minutes until tender, then stir in the spinach for 1 minute.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy and serve alongside.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C at the thickest part. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Egg Kari Mamak Malaysian Egg Curry
recipes.summary: Boiled eggs in a spiced tomato and coconut gravy, mopped up with rice.
steps: Hard-boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool and peel.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Fry the onion, garlic and ginger in the oil for 5 minutes until soft, then stir in the curry powder for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, coconut milk and water and simmer 12 minutes until thick.
Slide in the eggs, warm 3 minutes and serve with the rice.
notes: Food safety: hard-boil the eggs until the yolk is firm. Contains egg. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Kai Jeow Moo Sap Thai Pork Omelette Rice Bowl
recipes.summary: A puffy, crisp-edged omelette with minced pork over rice, drizzled with a salty-sweet sauce.
steps: Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the fish sauce and soy sauce and stir through the pork.
Heat the oil in a wok until shimmering and pour in the egg mix from a height.
Fry for 2 minutes per side until puffed, golden and the pork reaches 75°C, then drain on paper.
Serve over the rice with the sweet chilli sauce and cucumber.
notes: Food safety: cook the pork mince to 75°C and the eggs until set. Contains egg, fish, gluten and soy. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Mee Rebus Mamak Sweet Potato Gravy Noodles
recipes.summary: Yellow noodles in a thick sweet-potato and peanut gravy topped with egg, tofu and lime.
steps: Hard-boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool and peel.
Boil the sweet potato in the water for 12 minutes until soft, then blend with the peanuts, shallots and garlic.
Fry the curry powder in the oil for 1 minute, add the blended gravy and soy sauce and simmer 12 minutes until thick.
Boil the noodles until tender, about 4 minutes, and divide into bowls.
Pour over the gravy and top with halved egg, tofu and lime.
notes: Food safety: hard-boil the eggs until the yolk is firm. Contains egg, gluten, peanuts and soy. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Bun Rieu Cua Vietnamese Tomato Crab-Style Noodle Soup
recipes.summary: A tomato broth with soft prawn-and-egg cakes, tofu and rice noodles.

items: 400g raw prawns, peeled and finely chopped

steps: Mix the prawns, eggs and 1 tsp fish sauce into a paste.
Fry the shallots and tomatoes in the oil for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the water, tamarind and remaining fish sauce and bring to a simmer until steaming.
Drop spoonfuls of the prawn mix into the broth and simmer 8 minutes until the cakes float, are firm and pink, then add the tofu.
Cook the noodles until tender, about 4 minutes, and serve with broth, cakes and sprouts.
notes: Food safety: cook the prawn cakes until firm and pink, at least 63°C inside, and the eggs until set. Contains egg, fish, shellfish and soy. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Pho Ga Hanoi Chicken Noodle Soup
recipes.summary: A clear chicken broth with ginger, onion and star anise over rice noodles and herbs.
steps: Char the onion and ginger in a dry pan for 5 minutes.
Simmer the chicken with the onion, ginger, star anise and water for 40 minutes until the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Lift out the chicken, shred the meat and strain the broth, seasoning with fish sauce and 1 tsp salt.
Cook the noodles until tender, about 4 minutes, and divide into bowls.
Top with the chicken, ladle over the hot broth and serve with spring onion, coriander, sprouts and lime.
notes: Food safety: cook the chicken to 75°C at the thickest part. Contains fish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Cha Ca La Vong Turmeric Fish with Dill
recipes.summary: Hanoi turmeric fish seared with dill and spring onion, served over noodles with peanuts and fish dip.

items: 700g firm white fish fillet, cut into chunks

steps: Toss the fish with the turmeric, ginger and 1 tsp salt.
Cook the noodles until tender, about 4 minutes, and drain.
Stir the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and 2 tbsp water into a dip.
Sear the fish in the oil for 6 minutes until golden and opaque, flaking easily at 63°C.
Toss in the dill and spring onions for 1 minute, then serve over the noodles with peanuts and the dip.
notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, at least 63°C. Contains fish and peanuts. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Gaeng Hung Lay Northern Thai Pork Belly Curry
recipes.summary: A dry-spiced Chiang Mai pork curry with ginger and tamarind, sweet-sour and rich, with no coconut milk.
steps: Fry the curry paste in a dry heavy pot for 3 minutes, then add the pork and brown for 6 minutes.
Add the water, tamarind, sugar, fish sauce and soy sauce and simmer, covered, for 50 minutes until the pork is tender.
Add the ginger and garlic and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until the sauce is thick and the pork reaches 70°C.
Cook the rice until tender and fluffy, about 15 minutes.
Scatter the curry with peanuts and serve spooned over the rice with a little of the glossy sauce.
notes: Food safety: simmer the pork until tender and at least 70°C. Contains peanuts, fish, gluten, soy and shellfish. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.

recipes.title: Mie Aceh Spicy Curried Prawn Noodles
recipes.summary: Thick noodles in a spicy, curry-spiced tomato sauce with prawns, from the Sumatran coast.
steps: Blend the shallots, garlic and chillies to a paste.
Boil the noodles until tender, about 4 minutes, and drain.
Fry the paste and curry powder in the oil for 4 minutes, add the tomatoes and cook 4 minutes until soft.
Add the prawns, water and kecap manis and cook 4 minutes until the prawns turn pink and opaque.
Push to the side, scramble the eggs until set, toss in the noodles and sprouts for 2 minutes until hot and coated.
notes: Food safety: cook the prawns until pink and opaque, at least 63°C inside, and the eggs until set. Contains egg, gluten, shellfish and soy. Refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour.
